podcast.body: Bowie's attempt to rock harder, turning up the guitars and synthesizers to make his beats louder, though not necessarily edgier. However, the album delivered "airless digital rock" that failed to impress critics or fans, peaking at number 34 on the Billboard album chart (his lowest charter since "Heroes") and leaving Bowie with a "bad taste" in his mouth. "And on his next studio album, 1987's Never Let Me Down, he turned up the guitars and especially the syndromes, making his beats louder, if not necessarily edgier."
